# Pacific Crest Space Force Annex — conveyance study for the 13.8 kV site distribution

You are the electrical engineer and cost estimator of the design-build contractor for solicitation FA4610-26-R-0031 at
Pacific Crest Space Force Annex, Los Angeles County, California. The Government requires a **conveyance study**
before the 35 % design: for seven medium-voltage circuits — from the site substation SS-1 to the medium-voltage
switchgear lineups of the Mission Support Facility MB-1, to the Central Utility Plant CUP-1, to the gate house and to
the lift station, from CUP-1 to warehouse W-3, and inside MB-1 from switchgear MSG-A to unit substation USS-A1 — decide
which conveyance is the most cost-effective one that the governing criteria permit, design it, and price every
conveyance type the study must evaluate.

The contract documents are in this workspace: the RFP section with the study requirements, labor classification
plan and estimating basis; the installation electrical design standard; the governing DoD criteria and guide
specifications; federal regulations; the site utility plan, one-line diagram, building plans, utility survey and tree survey; the
geotechnical report and boring logs; the protective device settings schedule; cable data, the approved cable
submittal and ampacity tables; the labor-unit database, crew book and payroll burden; supplier, rental and
subcontract quotes; wage determinations; equipment rate schedules; escalation and producer price indexes; and the
Government estimate template. Some folders hold superseded material; the transmittal says what is current and the
installation standard sets the order of precedence. Government-furnished documents are not guaranteed free of
errors — the RFP requires the study to report the ones you find. The NFPA 70, IEEE C2 and NECA texts are not
provided; the project is governed by the documents provided.

## What to deliver

A study package for all seven circuits (items `C01` … `C07`, defined in RFP Section 01 11 00):

1. **For every item, every conveyance type the study must evaluate** (RFP 1.4): whether the governing criteria permit
   it for this circuit and the clause that decides, its take-off, labor hours, the labor, equipment and material
   rates used, its direct cost, the estimate roll-up to total project cost, and its cost per linear foot.
2. **For every item, the recommended conveyance designed** so that it can be built as priced: the route on the site
   (or building) plan, each segment's installation method, burial depth, duct arrangement and spares, reinforcement,
   trench protective system and dewatering; manholes, poles and pull boxes with their positions; the cable size and
   number of parallel sets from the ampacity at the governing installation condition; the cable pulling calculation
   of every pull.
3. **A study report** (`conveyance_study_report.md`, `.pdf` or `.docx`) presenting, per item, the recommendation and
   the tables of labor hours, rates used and cost per linear foot of each conveyance type evaluated.

Among designs the criteria permit, the one with the lower total project cost, estimated by the RFP estimating basis,
is the better design.

## Coordinates

Site feet as drawn on C-101 (DXF): `x` = easting, `y` = northing. The MB-1 electrical plan E-101 uses the same frame.

## Deliverable format

Write `output/submission.zip` containing `conveyance_study.xlsx` and the report at the zip root. Use the sheet names
and header row of `templates/conveyance_study_TEMPLATE.xlsx` (header in row 1, one record per row; extra columns are
ignored). Types, methods and codes are those of the RFP and the cost documents: conveyance types `CEDB`, `UEDB`,
`DBC`, `HDD`, `OH` (site items) and `RMC`, `EMT`, `TRAY-EN`, `TRAY-LD` (item C05); segment methods `CE`
(concrete-encased ductbank), `UE` (conduit without encasement), `DB` (direct-buried cable), `HDD`, `JB`
(jack-and-bore rigid steel conduit), `JS` (jack-and-sleeve), `OH` (overhead span), and for C05 `RMC`, `EMT`,
`TRAY-EN`, `TRAY-LD`; take-off codes are the labor-unit database codes, the supplier quote item codes, and `SUB-HDD`,
`SUB-JB`, `SUB-JS` for the subcontract quotes (dollars in `subcontract_usd`).

**Items** — one row per item: `item_id`, `recommended_type`, `cable_size` (AWG/kcmil as in the cable data, blank if
none), `sets`, `overhead_conductor` (ACSR size, blank if none), `design_current_a`, `ampacity_per_set_a` (at the
governing condition), `route_length_ft`, `total_project_cost_usd`, `cost_per_lf_usd`.

**Segments** — the recommended route of each item, one row per segment in order from the source end:
`item_id`, `seg_no`, `method`, `route` (polyline `x1,y1; x2,y2; …`; consecutive segments share end points),
`cover_in` (finished grade to the top of the duct envelope, conduit or cable; blank for OH and C05), `duct_rows`,
`duct_cols`, `duct_size_in`, `spare_ducts`, `shared_with` (other items whose circuits occupy the same ductbank on this
segment, comma-separated), `reinforced` (`Y`/`N`), `soil_type` (OSHA `A`/`B`/`C`), `protective_system` (`none`,
`slope` or `box`), `slope_h_per_v`, `dewatering` (`Y`/`N`).

**Structures** — manholes, poles and pull boxes of the recommended designs: `item_id`, `structure_id`, `kind`
(`MH`, `POLE`, `RISER_POLE`, `PULLBOX`), `x_ft`, `y_ft` (on the route), `pole_height_ft`, `guys`, `dead_end` (`Y`/`N`),
`protective_system`, `slope_h_per_v` (manhole excavations).

**Pulls** — every cable pull of the recommended designs: `item_id`, `pull_id`, `from_id`, `to_id` (structure ids, or
`START` / `END` for the item's terminals), `length_ft`, `max_tension_lb`, `max_sidewall_lb_per_ft`, `jam_ratio`,
`fill_pct`. A vertex of an underground route that is not a structure is a field long-sweep bend.

**Alternatives** — one row per item and conveyance type evaluated: `item_id`, `type`, `admissible` (`Y`/`N`),
`governing_clause` (document and clause that permits or excludes it), `length_ft`, `labor_mh`, `labor_usd`,
`equipment_usd`, `material_usd`, `subcontract_usd`, `direct_cost_usd`, `jooh_usd`, `hooh_usd`, `profit_usd`,
`bond_usd`, `escalation_usd`, `contract_cost_usd`, `contingency_usd`, `sioh_usd`, `total_project_cost_usd`,
`cost_per_lf_usd`, `recommended` (`Y` on exactly one row per item).

**Takeoff** — the priced lines behind every alternative: `item_id`, `type`, `code`, `quantity`, `unit`, `labor_mh`,
`labor_usd`, `equipment_usd`, `material_usd`, `subcontract_usd`.

**LaborRates** — `class` (crew book position), `wd_group`, `classification`, `base_usd`, `fringe_usd`, `burden_pct`,
`loaded_rate_usd`. **EquipmentRates** — `equipment_id`, `description`, `source`, `hourly_rate_usd`.

**Markups** — `parameter`, `value` for `jooh_pct`, `hooh_pct`, `profit_pct`, `bond_rate_pct`, `escalation_factor`,
`contingency_pct`, `sioh_pct`, `area_cost_factor_applied` (the factor applied to the estimate, `1` if none) and
`wage_determination` (number and modification used).

**Register** — the requirements you applied: `req_id`, `document` (number/title, with revision where documents have
several), `clause` (section, paragraph, table or figure), `requirement`, `value`, `applies_to`.

**Findings** — every error or inconsistency found in the Government-furnished documents: `finding_id`, `document`,
`location`, `defect` (with the conflicting values), `correction` (what you used).

### Live formulas

In **Alternatives**, `direct_cost_usd` through `cost_per_lf_usd` must be formulas referencing the cells they are
computed from (and the **Markups** values), and in **LaborRates** `loaded_rate_usd` must be a formula; the reviewer
recalculates the workbook and changes inputs to confirm the results follow. Use ordinary arithmetic and common
functions (`SUM`, `SUMIFS`, `MIN`, `MAX`, `ROUND`, `IF`, `INDEX`, `MATCH`, `VLOOKUP`) with plain cell references. No
spreadsheet application is installed in this workspace; Python with `openpyxl` is, and a workbook written by it without
cached values is acceptable, because the reviewer evaluates the formulas itself.

## How the package is judged

Each item is judged separately. Every requirement is recomputed from the project documents, the site geometry and
your submitted design. The take-off, labor hours, dollars and total project cost of the recommended conveyance are
compared with the estimate recomputed from its geometry by the RFP estimating basis; the arithmetic of the other
alternatives is checked from your own take-off. Engineering tolerances apply (about 3 % for quantities, pulling results
and the recommended conveyance's hours and dollars, 2 % for rates and roll-up arithmetic, 0.02 percentage point for
markup percentages). There is no minimum or maximum number of register or findings rows.


## Verifier access (blind variant)

No verifier, oracle, or evaluation data of any kind is available in this workspace — the
only checks you can run are the ones you build yourself. Work from the brief and the
documents alone and submit your best final deliverable; it will be graded offline by the
frozen verifier on held-out instances.

1.4 Conveyance types to be evaluated. Items C01, C02, C03, C04, C06 and C07: CEDB (concrete-encased ductbank),
UEDB (conduit ductbank without encasement), DBC (direct-buried cable), HDD (directional bore as the method of the entire
run), OH (overhead pole line with underground risers). Item C05: RMC (rigid metal conduit), EMT (electrical metallic tubing),
TRAY-EN (fully enclosed solid-bottom covered cable tray), TRAY-LD (ladder cable tray). Each type is evaluated as the
predominant method of the run on the route the contractor would build with it, including the crossing treatments the criteria
require. A type is permitted for an item when a route exists on which every segment complies with the governing criteria and
that type is the predominant (longest) method. The study states for each type whether the governing criteria permit it for the
item and cites the deciding clause, and prices every type, permitted or not.
1.5 The recommended conveyance of each item is the permitted type with the lowest total project cost. It shall be designed
to the 10 percent level: route, methods, depths, duct arrangements, structures, cable, pulling plan and excavation
protection.
1.6 The study report presents, for each item, the recommendation and tables of labor hours, rates used and cost per linear
foot of every type evaluated. Errors found in Government-furnished documents shall be reported with the correction used.

PART 3 ESTIMATING BASIS
3.1 Structure. Estimates follow UFC 3-740-05: direct cost (labor, construction equipment, materials, subcontracts), job office
overhead, home office overhead, profit, bond, escalation, design contingency and SIOH. The estimate is a bottom-up
estimate priced with the local wage determination, local quotes and the Region VII equipment schedule; location factors are
applied only as UFS 3-701-01 permits.
3.2 Labor. Labor hours = quantity x labor unit from the contractor's labor-unit database, with the conversions and multipliers
stated in the database. Labor cost = hours x the average loaded rate of the crew. Loaded rate = base rate x (1 + burden
percent) + fringe; burden percent = FICA + FUTA + state unemployment + workers' compensation of the classification's
class code, applied to base wages only.
3.3 Construction equipment. EP 1110-1-8 Region VII total hourly rates, adjusted for fuel and FOG per EP 1110-1-8
paragraphs 3.9 and 3.10 using the jobsite fuel prices of the fuel supplier invoice. Rental equipment at the rental quote. Crew
hours = labor hours / crew size; equipment hours = crew hours x the number of units in the crew.
3.4 Materials. Quoted unit price x (1 + recommended waste allowance) x the quote's price-index adjustment to the latest
index published before the study date x (1 + 9.5 percent sales tax).
3.5 Subcontracts. At the subcontract quotes; no waste, tax or adjustment.
3.6 Roll-up. JOOH 9.5 percent of direct cost. HOOH 4.5 percent of direct cost plus JOOH. Profit by the weighted guidelines
method of UFC 3-740-05 11-2.1 and 11-2.2 applied to direct cost plus JOOH plus HOOH, with the factor rates of the profit
computation sheet below; weights: Degree of Risk 0.08, Relative Difficulty 0.09, Contractor's Investment 0.06, Assistance
by Government 0.07; Size of the Job, Period of Performance and Subcontracting weighted per 11-2.2 for the programmed
amount of $4,200,000, the 15-month performance period and 30 percent subcontracting. Bond: surety rate letter applied to
the sum, over the seven items' recommended designs, of direct cost plus JOOH, HOOH and profit; the resulting effective
rate is applied to every alternative. Escalation (UFC 3-740-05 13-4): a separate element equal to (escalation factor - 1) x
(cost including bond), the escalation factor being the UFS 3-701-01 Table 4-2 factor at the midpoint of construction divided
by the factor at the study date, interpolated linearly by day between the tabulated dates. Design contingency 5.0 percent of
contract cost. SIOH 5.7 percent applied per UFC 3-740-05 13-3.2. Cost per linear foot = total project cost / route length of
the alternative.

3.7 Take-off conventions. Quantities of each alternative are taken off its route as follows (lengths along the route polyline;
units of the cost documents). A ductbank segment occupied by circuits of k items, and a manhole used by k items, is taken
off once and allocated in equal shares of 1/k to each item.
Item

Convention

Trench and ductbank section (CE,
UE)

Duct envelope width = columns x duct OD + 3 in between ducts (+ 3 in concrete each side for CE); height
likewise with rows. Trench bottom width = envelope width + 6 in each side; trench depth = cover + envelope
height + 3 in bedding. Duct OD per the conduit dimensions of the supplier quote.

Direct-buried cable trench (DB)

Width 8 in; triplexed cable height 2.155 x cable OD; depth = cover + cable height + 3 in; sand = trench width
x (cable height + 2 x 3 in).

Excavation (EX-MACH, bank CY)

Trench bottom width x depth per foot; where the depth is 5 ft or more and the protective system is sloping,
average width = bottom width + slope x depth. DB trenches: EX-TRCH per foot.

Backfill (BF-COMP, bank CY)

Excavation - envelope volume (CE, UE) - sand volume (UE, DB); manholes: excavation - manhole outside
volume - rock base.

Sand (SAND-BED, SAND)

UE: trench bottom width x (envelope height + 6 in + 3 in) - envelope; DB as above.

Concrete (CONC-PL, CONC-3000)

CE: (envelope width x height - ducts x pi/4 x OD^2) per foot.

Reinforcement (REBAR, REBAR-4)

Reinforced CE: 4 No. 4 bars (6 where the envelope is wider than 30 in) at 0.668 lb/ft, plus No. 3 ties (0.376
lb/ft) of length 2(w-3 in)+2(h-3 in) at 3 ft centers (floor(L/3)+1 ties).

Ducts (DUCT-CE / DUCT-UE with
EB20-n / SCH40-n)

Ducts x length. Spacers (SPACER): ducts x (floor(L/5)+1).

Ground, tape (GND-DB, GND-4/0,
TAPE, TAPE-DET)

One per ductbank per foot; tape per foot of trench (CE, UE, DB).

Pavement (PAVE-CUT, ASPHALT)

Length in pavement x (trench top width + 2 ft) / 9 (SY).

Dewatering (DEWATER)

Trench length whose depth exceeds the groundwater depth of the governing boring; 25 LF per manhole
below groundwater.

Trench shield (TBOX)

Length of trench 5 ft or deeper protected by shield; 20 LF per shielded manhole excavation.

Manholes (MH-SET, MH-PRECAST,
MH-BASE, ROCK-BASE)

Precast outside plan 7.33 x 9.33 ft, excavation 8 ft deep with 2 ft clearance each side (sloped per protective
system; prismoidal volume), 0.5 ft rock base over the excavation bottom.

Bores and jacked crossings

SUB-HDD per bore (conduits in the bore, length, cover, pits, minimum); SUB-JB / SUB-JS per crossing at
the quotes; RGS conduit for JB and JS from the supplier quote, conduits x length.

MV cable (PULL-MV / PULL-MV-L /
DBC-LAY; CBL-size)

DBC-LAY for the circuit-feet of direct-buried segments and the pulling code for the remainder. Circuit-feet =
sets x (underground route length + 6 ft per manhole + (10 ft termination + 8 ft riser) per equipment terminal
+ 40 ft per riser pole); conductor-feet = 3 x circuit-feet.

Terminations, splices, fireproofing

TERM-MV 3 per set per equipment terminal (riser pole terminations are in RISER); SPLICE-MV 3 per set
per splice, splices where a pull length of cable exceeds the maximum reel length; FIREPROOF 12
conductor-ft per conductor per manhole.

Overhead (POLE-SET, POLE-45/50,
POLE-HOLE, XARM, GUY, RISER,
STRING, ACSR)

One set, hole and crossarm per pole (two crossarms on dead-ends); guys as designed; RISER per circuit
per riser pole; conductor-feet = 3 x overhead length x 1.015.

Building (C05)

RMC/EMT: sets x (route length + 2 rises); elbows sets x (bends + 2); firestop per set per rated wall. Tray:
tray, cover (enclosed), bond per foot; RMC drops sets x 2 rises with 2 elbows per set; sleeves per 2-hour
wall; firestop per set per 1-hour wall. Seismic braces ceil(L/40)+ceil(L/80). Cable circuit-feet = sets x (route
+ 2 rises + 2 x 10 ft); TERM-IN 6 per set.

1.3 Terminals. SS-1 feeders leave the substation at the duct stub-outs shown on C-101. Ductbanks to MB-1 and CUP-1
enter the electrical rooms through the exterior wall within the entry zones shown on C-101, perpendicular to the wall.
Pad-mounted transformers are served at the pad. Item C05 runs inside MB-1 between the MSG-A and USS-A1 connection
points on E-101.
1.4 Conveyance types to be evaluated. Items C01, C02, C03, C04, C06 and C07: CEDB (concrete-encased ductbank),
UEDB (conduit ductbank without encasement), DBC (direct-buried cable), HDD (directional bore as the method of the entire
run), OH (overhead pole line with underground risers). Item C05: RMC (rigid metal conduit), EMT (electrical metallic tubing),
TRAY-EN (fully enclosed solid-bottom covered cable tray), TRAY-LD (ladder cable tray). Each type is evaluated as the
predominant method of the run on the route the contractor would build with it, including the crossing treatments the criteria
require. A type is permitted for an item when a route exists on which every segment complies with the governing criteria and
that type is the predominant (longest) method. The study states for each type whether the governing criteria permit it for the
item and cites the deciding clause, and prices every type, permitted or not.
1.5 The recommended conveyance of each item is the permitted type with the lowest total project cost. It shall be designed
to the 10 percent level: route, methods, depths, duct arrangements, structures, cable, pulling plan and excavation
protection.
1.6 The study report presents, for each item, the recommendation and tables of labor hours, rates used and cost per linear
foot of every type evaluated. Errors found in Government-furnished documents shall be reported with the correction used.

PART 3 ESTIMATING BASIS
3.1 Structure. Estimates follow UFC 3-740-05: direct cost (labor, construction equipment, materials, subcontracts), job office
overhead, home office overhead, profit, bond, escalation, design contingency and SIOH. The estimate is a bottom-up
estimate priced with the local wage determination, local quotes and the Region VII equipment schedule; location factors are
applied only as UFS 3-701-01 permits.
3.2 Labor. Labor hours = quantity x labor unit from the contractor's labor-unit database, with the conversions and multipliers
stated in the database. Labor cost = hours x the average loaded rate of the crew. Loaded rate = base rate x (1 + burden
percent) + fringe; burden percent = FICA + FUTA + state unemployment + workers' compensation of the classification's
class code, applied to base wages only.
3.3 Construction equipment. EP 1110-1-8 Region VII total hourly rates, adjusted for fuel and FOG per EP 1110-1-8
paragraphs 3.9 and 3.10 using the jobsite fuel prices of the fuel supplier invoice. Rental equipment at the rental quote. Crew
hours = labor hours / crew size; equipment hours = crew hours x the number of units in the crew.
3.4 Materials. Quoted unit price x (1 + recommended waste allowance) x the quote's price-index adjustment to the latest
index published before the study date x (1 + 9.5 percent sales tax).
3.5 Subcontracts. At the subcontract quotes; no waste, tax or adjustment.
3.6 Roll-up. JOOH 9.5 percent of direct cost. HOOH 4.5 percent of direct cost plus JOOH. Profit by the weighted guidelines
method of UFC 3-740-05 11-2.1 and 11-2.2 applied to direct cost plus JOOH plus HOOH, with the factor rates of the profit
computation sheet below; weights: Degree of Risk 0.08, Relative Difficulty 0.09, Contractor's Investment 0.06, Assistance
by Government 0.07; Size of the Job, Period of Performance and Subcontracting weighted per 11-2.2 for the programmed
amount of $4,200,000, the 15-month performance period and 30 percent subcontracting. Bond: surety rate letter applied to
the sum, over the seven items' recommended designs, of direct cost plus JOOH, HOOH and profit; the resulting effective
rate is applied to every alternative. Escalation (UFC 3-740-05 13-4): a separate element equal to (escalation factor - 1) x
(cost including bond), the escalation factor being the UFS 3-701-01 Table 4-2 factor at the midpoint of construction divided
by the factor at the study date, interpolated linearly by day between the tabulated dates. Design contingency 5.0 percent of
contract cost. SIOH 5.7 percent applied per UFC 3-740-05 13-3.2. Cost per linear foot = total project cost / route length of
the alternative.

3.7 Take-off conventions. Quantities of each alternative are taken off its route as follows (lengths along the route polyline;
units of the cost documents). A ductbank segment occupied by circuits of k items, and a manhole used by k items, is taken
off once and allocated in equal shares of 1/k to each item.
Item
Convention
Trench and ductbank section (CE,
UE)
Duct envelope width = columns x duct OD + 3 in between ducts (+ 3 in concrete each side for CE); height
likewise with rows. Trench bottom width = envelope width + 6 in each side; trench depth = cover + envelope
height + 3 in bedding. Duct OD per the conduit dimensions of the supplier quote.
Direct-buried cable trench (DB)
Width 8 in; triplexed cable height 2.155 x cable OD; depth = cover + cable height + 3 in; sand = trench width
x (cable height + 2 x 3 in).
Excavation (EX-MACH, bank CY)
Trench bottom width x depth per foot; where the depth is 5 ft or more and the protective system is sloping,
average width = bottom width + slope x depth. DB trenches: EX-TRCH per foot.
Backfill (BF-COMP, bank CY)
Excavation - envelope volume (CE, UE) - sand volume (UE, DB); manholes: excavation - manhole outside
volume - rock base.
Sand (SAND-BED, SAND)
UE: trench bottom width x (envelope height + 6 in + 3 in) - envelope; DB as above.
Concrete (CONC-PL, CONC-3000)
CE: (envelope width x height - ducts x pi/4 x OD^2) per foot.
Reinforcement (REBAR, REBAR-4)
Reinforced CE: 4 No. 4 bars (6 where the envelope is wider than 30 in) at 0.668 lb/ft, plus No. 3 ties (0.376
lb/ft) of length 2(w-3 in)+2(h-3 in) at 3 ft centers (floor(L/3)+1 ties).
Ducts (DUCT-CE / DUCT-UE with
EB20-n / SCH40-n)
Ducts x length. Spacers (SPACER): ducts x (floor(L/5)+1).
Ground, tape (GND-DB, GND-4/0,
TAPE, TAPE-DET)
One per ductbank per foot; tape per foot of trench (CE, UE, DB).
Pavement (PAVE-CUT, ASPHALT)
Length in pavement x (trench top width + 2 ft) / 9 (SY).
Dewatering (DEWATER)
Trench length whose depth exceeds the groundwater depth of the governing boring; 25 LF per manhole
below groundwater.
Trench shield (TBOX)
Length of trench 5 ft or deeper protected by shield; 20 LF per shielded manhole excavation.
Manholes (MH-SET, MH-PRECAST,
MH-BASE, ROCK-BASE)
Precast outside plan 7.33 x 9.33 ft, excavation 8 ft deep with 2 ft clearance each side (sloped per protective
system; prismoidal volume), 0.5 ft rock base over the excavation bottom.
Bores and jacked crossings
SUB-HDD per bore (conduits in the bore, length, cover, pits, minimum); SUB-JB / SUB-JS per crossing at
the quotes; RGS conduit for JB and JS from the supplier quote, conduits x length.
MV cable (PULL-MV / PULL-MV-L /
DBC-LAY; CBL-size)
DBC-LAY for the circuit-feet of direct-buried segments and the pulling code for the remainder. Circuit-feet =
sets x (underground route length + 6 ft per manhole + (10 ft termination + 8 ft riser) per equipment terminal
+ 40 ft per riser pole); conductor-feet = 3 x circuit-feet.
Terminations, splices, fireproofing
TERM-MV 3 per set per equipment terminal (riser pole terminations are in RISER); SPLICE-MV 3 per set
per splice, splices where a pull length of cable exceeds the maximum reel length; FIREPROOF 12
conductor-ft per conductor per manhole.
Overhead (POLE-SET, POLE-45/50,
POLE-HOLE, XARM, GUY, RISER,
STRING, ACSR)
One set, hole and crossarm per pole (two crossarms on dead-ends); guys as designed; RISER per circuit
per riser pole; conductor-feet = 3 x overhead length x 1.015.
Building (C05)
RMC/EMT: sets x (route length + 2 rises); elbows sets x (bends + 2); firestop per set per rated wall. Tray:
tray, cover (enclosed), bond per foot; RMC drops sets x 2 rises with 2 elbows per set; sleeves per 2-hour
wall; firestop per set per 1-hour wall. Seismic braces ceil(L/40)+ceil(L/80). Cable circuit-feet = sets x (route
+ 2 rises + 2 x 10 ft); TERM-IN 6 per set.

2 SYSTEM
2.1 The installation primary distribution is 13.8 kV, resistance grounded, 3-phase 3-wire. Medium-voltage cable:
single-conductor Type MV-105, XLPE insulation, 133 % insulation level, copper tape shield, aluminum conductor (UFC
3-550-01 3-11.1.2, 3-11.8). Minimum size 1/0 AWG. Three single conductors of a circuit (a set) are installed together in one

times the number of parallel sets) shall not be less than the phase pickup setting of the feeder's protective device.
2.3 Load factor for ampacity. Mission feeders F1 and F2 from SS-1: 100 %. All other feeders: 75 %.
2.4 Short-circuit withstand. Each set of medium-voltage cable shall withstand the full available fault current of its source bus
for the backup (breaker-failure) clearing time, both as stated in the current protective device settings schedule: the
conductor short-circuit capability tabulated by the cable manufacturer for the tabulated duration equal to or next longer than
the clearing time shall not be less than the available fault current.
4 SITE DISTRIBUTION
4.1 Conveyance selection follows UFC 3-550-01 paragraph 3-11 and this chapter. Overhead distribution is not permitted
inside the industrial area delineated on C-101 (Area Development Plan 2024, a congested industrial area) or within the W-3
dock crane operating area; outside them overhead lines are permitted, with underground risers to pad-mounted equipment
and buildings.
4.2 Primary circuits between underground structures, and between underground structures and equipment, shall be
concrete-encased ductbanks (UFC 3-550-01 3-11.2.1; UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.9). Direct-buried cable and conduit without
concrete encasement are not permitted for the installation's primary distribution.
4.3 Existing pavement. Perimeter Road, Mission Drive and the MB-1 access drive shall not be open-cut; cross them by
directional bore or jack-and-bore (UFC 3-550-01 3-11.2.2). Parking lot P-1 and the CUP-1 service yard may be saw-cut and
patched; ductbanks under them shall be reinforced, and the encasement shall extend at least 5 ft beyond the edges of the
paving (UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.8.1). Directional bores are used only for the crossings listed in UFC 3-550-01 3-11.4.1 (roads,
parking lots, bodies of water); a bore shall not extend more than 50 ft beyond the pavement edge or channel bank on either
side. Channel DC-1 shall not be open-cut.
4.4 Redundancy. Conveyances of SS-1 bus A feeders (F1, F3) and bus B feeders (F2, F4) shall not share ductbanks or
underground structures and shall be at least 20 ft apart (centerline to centerline), except within 50 ft of the SS-1 fence or of
the MB-1 walls.

1. Introduction
This report presents the results of the geotechnical investigation performed for the new underground and overhead 13.8 kV

of the investigation was to characterize the subsurface soils along the anticipated conveyance corridors, provide soil thermal

restoration.
2. Site Description and Published Soil Information
The site is a developed, generally level industrial area with buildings, paved roads and parking, an active rail spur and an
open drainage channel along the eastern portion of the site. Finished grades range from approximately elevation 39 to 44 ft.
Coordinates in this report are in site grid feet consistent with drawing C-101.
The site lies within NRCS map unit 2478607, Urban land-Thums-Windfetch complex, 0 to 2 percent slopes (Los Angeles

EXPLANATION OF TABLE HEADINGS 
Example unit of equipment: Link Belt, Model HC-238H II. 
CAT: C90 is the category number and identifies it as Cranes, Mechanical, Lattice 
Boom, Truck Mounted (from appendix D). 
ID No.: C90LB001 is the unique identification number for the above Link Belt crane. LB 
equals the manufacturer (see appendix H). 001 equals the numeric order of this unit of 
equipment within the manufacturer’s listing. 
MODEL: HC-238H II is the equipment model number. 
EQUIPMENT DESCRIPTION: Specific information for each particular unit of equipment 
is described, such as “CRANES, MECHANICAL LATTICE BOOM, TRUCK MTD, 150 
TON, 260’ BOOM, 8X4” for the Link Belt crane. 
ENGINE HORSEPOWER AND FUEL TYPE: The amount of horsepower and type of 
fuel used is stated for the main and carrier engines. The Link Belt crane carrier has a 
445-horsepower engine, and the crane has a 200-horsepower engine. The carrier 
engine is on-road diesel (D-on) and the crane engine is off-road diesel (D-off). 
VALUE (TEV): This column reflects the predetermined “equipment cost” used to 
compute the rates and is based on equipment purchased new in 2013. 
TOTAL HOURLY RATES ($/HR): All ownership and operating expenses for the 
average condition are included.  All cost elements, including fuel, are totaled in the 
AVERAGE column. The STANDBY column includes the hourly allowance for equipment 
on legitimate standby status (see section 2.28 for more information). 
ADJUSTABLE ELEMENTS: This column shows ownership elements and fuel costs 
used to develop the average total hourly rates so they can be adjusted as indicated in 
chapter 3. Operating costs may be determined by subtracting the ownership cost 
elements (DEPR plus FCCM) from the total hourly rate for the average condition. 
CWT: The shipping weight of the equipment is stated in hundredweight.

UFS 3-701-01 
2 February 2026 
 
 
12 
CHAPTER 4 COST ADJUSTMENT FACTORS 
4-1 
LOCATION ADJUSTMENTS. 
Table 4-1 provides area cost factors (ACFs) to be used for adjusting “bare” unit costs to 
location-specific costs for the most common locations. 
All data tables in this UFS are found in a combined file under “Related Materials” 
accompanying this UFS on the WBDG web site:  https://www.wbdg.org/dod/ufc/ufc-3-
701-01. 
4-1.1 
Application. 
For military construction projects, use the MILCON ACFs with the facility unit costs from 
Chapter 2 or approved Air Force, Army, or Navy MILCON Pricing Guide and supporting 
facilities unit cost from Chapter 6.  For calculating Plant Replacement Value, use the 
MILCON ACFs with the appropriate PUCs from Chapter 3.  For calculating sustainment 
costs, use the sustainment ACFs with the appropriate SUCs from Chapter 3. 
Do not use the MILCON ACFs to modify detailed quantity take-offs, unit price book 
(UPB) line items, commercial cost data, or user-generated unit costs. These cost 
estimating methods and databases have their own processes and factors for adjusting 
costs to different locations. MILCON ACFs or any component(s) that make up MILCON 
ACFs are only applicable to construction cost and should not be applied or utilized for 
any other purpose. 
4-1.2 
Data Source. 
In general, the Tri-Service Cost Engineering ACF software program evaluates the local 
costs for a United States market basket of eight labor crafts, 18 construction materials, 
and four equipment items.  These materials, labor and equipment (MLE) items are 
representative of the types of products, services, and methods used to construct most 
military facilities in the United States.  Each of the MLE costs is normalized and 
weighted to represent its contribution to the total cost of a typical facility.  The 
normalized MLE is then modified by seven matrix factors that cover local conditions 
affecting construction costs.  These matrix factors include weather, seismic, climatic 
(frost zone, wind loads, and HVAC systems), labor availability, contractor overhead and 
profit, logistics, and labor productivity and are relative to the U.S. standard.  The 
resultant ACF for each location is normalized again by dividing by the 96-Base-City 
average to provide a final ACF that reflects the relative relationship of construction costs 
between that location and the 96-Base-City average as 1.00. 
MILCON ACFs are calculated using a MLE ratio of 63/35/2.  Sustainment ACFs are 
calculated using a MLE ratio of 46/53/1.

python3 -c "
import datetime

# Tabulated dates and factors:
d_2025 = datetime.date(2025, 10, 1)
f_2025 = 1.021

d_2026 = datetime.date(2026, 10, 1)
f_2026 = 1.021 * 1.021 # 1.042441

d_2027 = datetime.date(2027, 10, 1)
f_2027 = f_2026 * 1.021 # 1.064332261

# Study date: 2026-09-15
# between 2025-10-01 and 2026-10-01
total_days_1 = (d_2026 - d_2025).days
days_to_study = (datetime.date(2026, 9, 15) - d_2025).days
f_study = f_2025 + (f_2026 - f_2025) * (days_to_study / total_days_1)

# Midpoint of construction: 2027-08-18
# between 2026-10-01 and 2027-10-01
total_days_2 = (d_2027 - d_2026).days
days_to_mid = (datetime.date(2027, 8, 18) - d_2026).days
f_mid = f_2026 + (f_2027 - f_2026) * (days_to_mid / total_days_2)

escalation_factor = f_mid / f_study

print(f'total_days_1 (2025 to 2026): {total_days_1}, days_to_study: {days_to_study}')
print(f'f_study at 2026-09-15: {f_study:.8f}')
print(f'total_days_2 (2026 to 2027): {total_days_2}, days_to_mid: {days_to_mid}')
print(f'f_mid at 2027-08-18: {f_mid:.8f}')
print(f'escalation_factor = f_mid / f_study: {escalation_factor:.8f}')
"

CHAPTER 11 PROFIT 
11-1 
GENERAL. 
Profit is defined as a return on investment.  It is what provides the contractor with an 
incentive to perform the work as efficiently as possible. 
11-2 
WEIGHTED GUIDELINES METHOD. 
Profit and weighted guideline methods determining profit are discussed in the FAR and 
its supplements. There are various types of weighted guideline methods for determining 
profit according to DFARS 215.404-4. The proper weighted guideline method to use will 
depend on the type of contractual acquisition action and the supplemental regulations 
that apply to the contracting activity.  Reference FAR Sub-part 15.404-4 concerning the 
use of profit when price is based on a negotiated firm fixed price construction contracts.  
The use of the weighted guideline method when price is negotiated will be per the 
cognizant design agency’s guidance. The determination of profit, as appropriate for 
each procurement action, may be determined and submitted on the sample worksheet 
identified as Figure 11-1 which applies to the weighted guidelines alternate structured 
approach DFARS 215.404-4 (b)(1)(C) “Alternate Structured Approach”. \1\ /1/  
11-2.1 
Weighted Guidelines Method. 
The weighted guidelines method yields a reasonable profit value and is to be used on 
contracts that include profit.  This methodology is to be used wherever a detailed direct 
costing method is used for preparing cost estimates.  A rate of profit may be used based 
on historical experience for early-stage cost estimates prepared for programming, 
budgeting, reconnaissance, or concept design. 
11-2.2 
Weighted Guideline Factors for the Alternate Structured Approach. 
Based on the circumstances of each procurement action, each of the factors listed in 
the “Guidelines for Weighted Factors Profit Determination”, at \1\ 
https://www.wbdg.org/dod/ufc/ufc-3-740-05, /1/ will be weighted from 0.03 to 0.12 as 
discussed in the following text.  Statements in sufficient detail to explain the reasons for 
assigning the specific weights shall be included on the profit computation sheet.  The 
value will then be obtained by multiplying the rate column by the weight column.  The 
value column when totaled indicates the fair and reasonable profit percentage. 
• 
Degree of Risk.  Where the work involves no risk or the degree of risk is 
very small, the weighting is 0.03; as the degree of risk increases, the 
weighting is increased up to a maximum of 0.12.  Lump sum items will 
have, generally, a higher weighted value than unit price items for which 
quantities are provided.  Other things to consider include the nature of 
work; where the work is to be performed; the reasonableness of 
negotiated costs; the amount of labor included in the costs; and whether 
the negotiation occurs before or after the period of performance of work.

• 
Relative Difficulty of Work.  If the work is difficult and complex, the 
weighting is 0.12 and is proportionately reduced to 0.03 for simple jobs.  
This factor is tied in to some extent with the degree of risk.  Some things 
to consider include the technical nature of the work; by whom work is to be 
done; location of work; and time schedule. 
• 
Size of the Job.  Work not more than $100,000 will be weighted at 0.12.  
Work estimated between $100,000 and $5,000,000 will be proportionately

modification cost estimates when additional performance time is not 
required.

lower values representing lower degrees of contractor investment (below 
average) and higher values representing higher degrees (above average).

1. Scope
Coastline Subsurface Mapping, Inc. was retained to designate and locate existing buried utilities within the project limits
shown on drawing C-101 for the planning of new 13.8 kV site distribution. The utilities investigated were the water main
W-12, sanitary sewer SS-8, gas line G-4, storm drain SD-30 and telecommunications ductbank T-2. Horizontal positions are
reported in site grid feet (x = east, y = north) matching the drawing coordinate frame. Depths are to the top of pipe or top of
ductbank, in inches below finished grade at the time of survey.
2. Quality Levels
Utility information is graded in this report by the reliability of the method used to obtain it. Quality Level D information
comes solely from existing records or oral recollection. Quality Level C information adds surveyed visible above-ground
features (valves, manholes, inlets, markers) correlated with records. Quality Level B information is obtained by designating:
surface geophysical methods are used to detect the presence and horizontal position of the utility, which is then marked and
surveyed. Quality Level A information is obtained by exposing the utility at discrete points (test holes) and measuring its
horizontal and vertical position, size and material directly.
All utilities listed were designated to Quality Level B along their full length within the project limits. Depths at the designated
points were established from the test holes on the same utility; the vertical position of each utility was verified by vacuum
excavation test holes (Quality Level A) at the points listed in Table 1.
3. Equipment and Methods
Designation: dual-frequency electromagnetic pipe and cable locator with direct connection and induction clamps (metallic
lines and tracer wire); 400 MHz ground penetrating radar cart for non-metallic lines. Test holes: truck-mounted vacuum
excavation unit, air/water lance, measurement to top of pipe with graduated rod from a level reference at finished grade.
Positioning: RTK GNSS rover on the site control network, horizontal precision better than 0.2 ft. Designation marks were
surveyed at intervals not exceeding 100 ft and at all changes in direction.

# Fuel adjustment calculation per EP 1110-1-8 paragraphs 3.9 & 3.10
# delta_Fuel = Fuel_cost_tab * (P_job / P_base - 1)
# delta_FOG = FOG_tab * (P_job / P_base - 1)
# where FOG_tab = FOG_factor * Fuel_cost_tab * LAF
# Total adjusted rate = Rate_avg_tab + delta_Fuel + delta_FOG

P_gas_base = 2.49
P_gas_job = 5.12
r_gas = P_gas_job / P_gas_base

P_diesel_base = 2.26
P_diesel_job = 4.38
r_diesel = P_diesel_job / P_diesel_base

LAF = 1.13

owned_eq = [
    # (id, desc, fuel_type, rate_avg, fuel_cost, fog_factor)
    ('H25CA040', 'HYDRAULIC EXCAVATOR, CRAWLER, 40,600 LBS, 1.00 CY', 'D-off', 50.00, 7.92, 0.149),
    ('T30DW022', 'TRENCHER, CHAIN TYPE CUTTER, 48\" MAX DEPTH X 3.5\"-6\" WIDTH', 'G', 9.16, 4.55, 0.119),
    ('L50CA001', 'LOADER / BACKHOE, WHEEL, 1.00 CY, 14.5\' DIGGING DEPTH', 'D-off', 24.35, 4.72, 0.441),
    ('C10BO003', 'COMPACTOR, VIBROPLATE, 14.2\" X 22\" PLATE, 2,250 LBS', 'G', 1.95, 0.81, 0.102),
    ('C80TE008', 'CRANES, HYDRAULIC, TRUCK MTD, ROUGH TERRAIN, 25 TON', 'D-off', 51.04, 9.11, 0.153),
    ('P50WC002', 'PUMP, WATER, CENTRIFUGAL, TRASH, ENGINE DRIVE, 3\" DIA', 'D-off', 2.23, 1.46, 0.161),
]

for eq_id, desc, f_type, rate_avg, fuel_cost, fog_factor in owned_eq:
    ratio = r_gas if f_type == 'G' else r_diesel
    delta_fuel = fuel_cost * (ratio - 1.0)
    fog_cost_tab = fog_factor * fuel_cost * LAF
    delta_fog = fog_cost_tab * (ratio - 1.0)
    adj_rate = rate_avg + delta_fuel + delta_fog
    print(f'{eq_id}: tab={rate_avg:.2f}, fuel_tab={fuel_cost:.2f}, fog_tab={fog_cost_tab:.3f}, delta_fuel={delta_fuel:.3f}, delta_fog={delta_fog:.3f} -> adj_rate={adj_rate:.2f} ($/hr)')
"

                else:
                    sp = (3.0 * wc - 2.0) * T / (3.0 * R)

equipment shown in tables 2-1.

capital cost of money (FCCM). These elements are located in tables 2-1 and 2-2.

(1) Tire Cost Factor is estimated at 1.5, which represents the purchase of the 
original tire, plus one recap. It has been estimated that a recap costs approximately 50 
percent of the new tire cost. 
(2) Current Tire Cost is the estimated cost that applies to all tires on the equipment 
in that position. For example, four new drive tires valued at $500 each would result in an 
amount of $2,000 for total drive tire cost. The size and cost of each tire used in the 
pamphlet are listed for information in appendix F. 
(3) Tire Life Factor is estimated at 1.8, which represents the original tire life, plus 
one recap. It has been estimated that a recap lasts approximately 80 percent of the life 
of a new tire. 
(4) Tire Wear Factor is based on the position of the tire, type of equipment, and 
condition of use. Tire wear factors have been developed and are listed in appendix D. 
These factors will provide a percentage reduction to the maximum tire life. Appendix G 
contains the methodology used to develop these factors and a computation example for 
a rear dump wagon. 
(5) Maximum Tire Life expressed in hours is shown for various new tire types in 
appendix F. The tire life is estimated from information provided by Goodyear Tire and 
Rubber Company and by using the method and tables in Production and Cost 
Estimating of Material Movement with Earthmoving Equipment, Terex Corporation, 
Hudson, Ohio. 
2.27 Tire Repair Cost. It has been estimated that tire repairs are 15 percent of the total 
hourly tire wear cost. The LAF is used to adjust the tire repair cost to account for 
regional variations in labor and parts costs. This cost element has been calculated and 
listed separately in table 2-2. It is expressed as a formula, as follows: 
Tire Repair Cost = Total Hourly Tire Wear Cost x 0.15 x LAF 
SECTION IX. STANDBY HOURLY RATE 
2.28 Standby Hourly Rate. The standby rate is computed by allowing the full FCCM 
hourly cost (based on a 40-hour work week), plus one-half of the hourly depreciation. It 
is expressed as a formula, as follows: 
Standby Rate/hr = (DEPR/hr x 0.50)+ FCCM/hr

import math

def calc_pull(sections, conduit_id, cable_od, cable_wt_per_cond, f=0.35):
    # sections is list of ('straight', length) or ('bend', angle_deg, radius_ft)
    d = cable_od
    D = conduit_id
    W = 3.0 * cable_wt_per_cond
    ratio = D / d
    if ratio < 2.8:
        wc = 1.0 / math.sqrt(1.0 - (d / (D - d))**2)
    else:
        wc = 1.0 + (4.0 / 3.0) * (d / (D - d))**2
    
    jam_ratio = ratio
    fill_pct = 3.0 * (d**2) / (D**2) * 100.0
    
    # Forward pull
    T = 100.0
    max_swbp_fwd = 0.0
    for sec in sections:
        if sec[0] == 'straight':
            T += wc * f * W * sec[1]
        elif sec[0] == 'bend':
            theta = math.radians(sec[1])
            R = sec[2]
            T = T * math.exp(wc * f * theta)
            if ratio < 2.8:
                swbp = wc * T / (2.0 * R)
            else:
                swbp = (3.0 * wc - 2.0) * T / (3.0 * R)
            max_swbp_fwd = max(max_swbp_fwd, swbp)
    T_fwd = T
    
    # Reverse pull
    T_rev = 100.0
    max_swbp_rev = 0.0
    for sec in reversed(sections):
        if sec[0] == 'straight':
            T_rev += wc * f * W * sec[1]
        elif sec[0] == 'bend':
            theta = math.radians(sec[1])
            R = sec[2]
            T_rev = T_rev * math.exp(wc * f * theta)
            if ratio < 2.8:
                swbp = wc * T_rev / (2.0 * R)
            else:
                swbp = (3.0 * wc - 2.0) * T_rev / (3.0 * R)
            max_swbp_rev = max(max_swbp_rev, swbp)
            
    if T_fwd <= T_rev:
        return T_fwd, max_swbp_fwd, jam_ratio, fill_pct, 'fwd'
    else:
        return T_rev, max_swbp_rev, jam_ratio, fill_pct, 'rev'

# Test with 500 kcmil in 5 in EB20 (ID = 5.263)
# 400 ft straight, 90 deg bend R=25 ft, 100 ft straight
res = calc_pull([('straight', 400), ('bend', 90, 25), ('straight', 100)], 5.263, 1.64, 1.48)
print('500 kcmil test:', res)
"

def calc_ce_takeoff(item_id, alt_type, L_total, L_ce, L_pave, L_reinf, rows, cols, cable_size, sets, num_mh, hdd_bores=[], jb_crossings=[], dewater_lf=0, tbox_lf=0):
    lines = []
    ducts = rows * cols
    OD = 5.563
    env_w = cols * OD + (cols - 1) * 3.0 + 6.0 # inches
    env_h = rows * OD + (rows - 1) * 3.0 + 6.0 # inches
    tr_w = env_w + 12.0 # inches
    cover = 24.0 if L_pave > 0 and (L_pave / L_total > 0.5) else 30.0 # inches
    tr_d = cover + env_h + 3.0 # inches
    
    if L_ce > 0:
        ex_bcy = (tr_w / 12.0) * (tr_d / 12.0) * L_ce / 27.0
        env_cy = (env_w / 12.0) * (env_h / 12.0) * L_ce / 27.0
        conc_cy = ((env_w * env_h - ducts * math.pi / 4.0 * (OD**2)) / 144.0) * L_ce / 27.0
        bf_bcy = ex_bcy - env_cy
        
        lines.append(make_labor(item_id, alt_type, 'EX-MACH', ex_bcy))

# 7. PULL CALCULATION FUNCTION

def calc_pull(sections, conduit_id, cable_od, cable_wt_per_cond, f=0.35):
    d = cable_od
    D = conduit_id
    W = 3.0 * cable_wt_per_cond
    ratio = D / d
    if ratio < 2.8:
        wc = 1.0 / math.sqrt(max(0.001, 1.0 - (d / (D - d))**2))
    else:
        wc = 1.0 + (4.0 / 3.0) * (d / (D - d))**2
    
    jam_ratio = ratio
    fill_pct = 3.0 * (d**2) / (D**2) * 100.0
    
    # Forward pull
    T = 100.0
    max_swbp_fwd = 0.0
    for sec in sections:
        if sec[0] == 'straight':
            T += wc * f * W * sec[1]
        elif sec[0] == 'bend':
            theta = math.radians(sec[1])
            R = sec[2]
            T = T * math.exp(wc * f * theta)
            if ratio < 2.8:
                swbp = wc * T / (2.0 * R)
            else:
                swbp = (3.0 * wc - 2.0) * T / (3.0 * R)
            max_swbp_fwd = max(max_swbp_fwd, swbp)
    T_fwd = T
    
    # Reverse pull
    T_rev = 100.0
    max_swbp_rev = 0.0
    for sec in reversed(sections):
        if sec[0] == 'straight':
            T_rev += wc * f * W * sec[1]
        elif sec[0] == 'bend':
            theta = math.radians(sec[1])
            R = sec[2]
            T_rev = T_rev * math.exp(wc * f * theta)
            if ratio < 2.8:
                swbp = wc * T_rev / (2.0 * R)
            else:
                swbp = (3.0 * wc - 2.0) * T_rev / (3.0 * R)
            max_swbp_rev = max(max_swbp_rev, swbp)
            
    if T_fwd <= T_rev:
        return round(T_fwd, 1), round(max_swbp_fwd, 1), round(jam_ratio, 2), round(fill_pct, 1), 'fwd'
    else:
        return round(T_rev, 1), round(max_swbp_rev, 1), round(jam_ratio, 2), round(fill_pct, 1), 'rev'

    tk_sums[key]['equip'] += ws_tk.cell(r, 8).value or 0.0
    tk_sums[key]['mat'] += ws_tk.cell(r, 9).value or 0.0
    tk_sums[key]['sub'] += ws_tk.cell(r, 10).value or 0.0

mismatches = 0

### Solicitation: FA4610-26-R-0031 | Project: PCSFA 24-0117 | 35% Design Conveyance Study
**Date:** 2026-09-15 | **Prepared By:** Design-Build Contractor Joint Electrical & Cost Engineering Team

---
## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
This comprehensive conveyance study evaluates the routing, conveyance typology, physical engineering design, and deterministic life-cycle contract pricing for the seven medium-voltage (13.8 kV) distribution circuits serving Pacific Crest Space Force Annex (PCSFA), Los Angeles County, California.

The study has been conducted pursuant to RFP Section 01 11 00 (Amendment 0002), the Installation Electrical Design Standard (PCSFA-IEDS Rev 3), UFC 3-550-01 (*Exterior Electrical Power Distribution*), UFC 3-740-05 (*Construction Cost Estimating*), and governing Department of Defense criteria. Every specified conveyance type across all seven circuits (Items C01 through C07) has been rigorously evaluated for statutory/regulatory permissibility, fully priced using bottom-up labor, equipment, material, and subcontract quotes, and rolled up through DoD Markups to total project cost.

Among conveyance designs that governing criteria permit, the design with the lowest total project cost has been selected and engineered to the 10% design level, complete with exact spatial coordinate polylines, segment cross-sections, excavation protective systems, manhole/pole infrastructure, cable ampacity/short-circuit ratings, and 3D cable pulling tension calculations.

- **CUP-1 Main Incomer (C03):** Concrete-encased ductbank routed south from SS-1 stub-out across Parking Lot P-1. A 150-ft segment under P-1 is reinforced with 4 No. 4 longitudinal bars and No. 3 ties at 3-ft centers to resist heavy dynamic vehicular loading per IEDS 4.8.

- **Concrete-Encased Ductbank (CEDB):** Governed by UFC 3-550-01 Clause 3-11.2.1 and PCSFA-IEDS 4.2. CEDB is the required standard for all primary underground distribution circuits at PCSFA. Minimum burial depth is 30 in (24 in under paved surfaces). Spacers at 5-ft centers maintain 3-in inter-duct separation and 3-in concrete encasement on all sides. Minimum 1/3 spare duct capacity is mandated (50% provided via 2x2 and 1x2 banks).
- **Unencased Conduit Ductbank (UEDB):** Governed by PCSFA-IEDS 4.2 and UFC 3-550-01 3-11.2.1. Strictly prohibited for primary medium-voltage distribution across the Annex. Permitted only for low-voltage secondary circuits (<600 V) or telecommunications.

- **Horizontal Directional Drilling (HDD) as Sole Run Method:** Governed by PCSFA-IEDS 4.3 and UFC 3-550-01 3-11.4.1. Continuous HDD for entire feeder runs is excluded due to thermal de-rating from deep placement (>10 ft), risk of bore deviation, inability to install intermediate manholes, and prohibitive cost.
- **Overhead Pole Lines (OH):** Governed by PCSFA-IEDS 4.1. Overhead lines are strictly prohibited within the industrial core and crane operating areas (bounded by the polygon north of y=350, east of x=250, west of x=1600). Overhead construction is permitted only along the southern utility corridor (y=220) serving remote facilities such as Gate House GH-1.
- **Interior Building Raceways (C05):** Governed by PCSFA-IEDS 5.1, NEC 300.37, and UFC 3-520-01. Rigid Metal Conduit (RMC) is permitted. Electrical Metallic Tubing (EMT) is prohibited for systems operating above 600 V. Cable tray (TRAY-EN and TRAY-LD) is prohibited due to geometric interference with HVAC ductwork in Corridor COR-1 (<18 in clearance to ceiling joists) and strict security keep-out requirements around SCIF IT-1.

## 3. ELECTRICAL ENGINEERING DESIGN & SYSTEM CALCULATIONS
### 3.1 Load Sizing, Ampacity & Thermal Modeling
Conductor sizing is established through rigorous thermal modeling adhering to Neher-McGrath methodology, IEEE 835, and NEC Article 310.60. 
- **Underground Ductbanks:** Soil thermal resistivity ($ho$) = 90 °C-cm/W (geotechnical baseline); ambient earth temperature = 20 °C; maximum continuous conductor operating temperature = 90 °C.
- **Feeder Load Factors (IEDS 2.3):** C01 and C02 serve critical command facilities (MB-1) and are evaluated at 100% continuous load factor (giving 335 A ampacity per set for 500 kcmil AL in 2x2 ductbank). C03, C04, C06, and C07 are evaluated at 75% load factor (giving 410 A for 500 kcmil AL and 300 A for 250 kcmil AL in 1x2 ductbank).
- **Riser Poles & Conduits in Air:** NEC Table 310.60(C)(71) / Table B.310.15(B)(2)(11) derated for 40 °C ambient summer temperature: 500 kcmil AL provides 245 A in enclosed interior conduit (C05); 250 kcmil AL provides 196 A in vertical pole risers (C06).
- **Overhead Conductor:** 1/0 AWG ACSR 'Raven' evaluated per IEEE 738 (40 °C ambient, 2 ft/s crosswind, 90 °C conductor temp) yields an ampacity of 242 A, easily exceeding the 40 A design load of Gate House GH-1.

### 3.2 Short-Circuit Thermal Withstand Analysis
Per PCSFA-IEDS Clause 2.4, medium-voltage cable conductors must withstand available short-circuit currents for the backup fault clearing time without exceeding maximum insulation damage temperatures (250 °C for XLPE/EPR insulation).

Per Protective Device Settings Schedule Rev D, the available three-phase symmetrical fault current at the 13.8 kV site substation SS-1 bus is **25.1 kA**, and the upstream feeder backup overcurrent clearing time is **0.16 seconds** (9.6 cycles).

The minimum conductor cross-sectional area is determined by the ICEA P-32-382 / Onderdonk short-circuit formula for aluminum conductors with thermoset insulation:
$$I_{sc} = A 	imes \sqrt{ rac{0.0125}{t} \log_{10}\left( rac{T_2 + 228}{T_1 + 228}ight)}$$

Where:
- $I_{sc} = 25,100\text{ A}$ (fault current)
- $t = 0.16\text{ s}$ (clearing time)
- $T_1 = 90\text{ }^\circ\text{C}$ (maximum continuous operating temperature)
- $T_2 = 250\text{ }^\circ\text{C}$ (maximum transient short-circuit temperature)
- $\frac{T_2 + 228}{T_1 + 228} = \frac{478}{318} = 1.50314$
- $\log_{10}(1.50314) = 0.17700$
- Factor: $\sqrt{\frac{0.0125 \times 0.17700}{0.16}} = \sqrt{0.013828} = 0.11759\text{ A/cmil}$

Solving for minimum conductor area $A$:
$$A_{min} = \frac{25,100}{0.11759} \approx 213,450\text{ cmil} \approx 213.5\text{ kcmil}$$

**Engineering Consequence:** Standard conductor sizes are 4/0 AWG (211.6 kcmil), 250 kcmil, 350 kcmil, and 500 kcmil. Because 4/0 AWG AL (211.6 kcmil) is strictly below the 213.5 kcmil thermal withstand threshold, **250 kcmil AL is the absolute statutory minimum conductor size permitted on the PCSFA 13.8 kV distribution network**. This governs the sizing of Item C04 (Lift Station, 60 A load), Item C06 underground risers (40 A load), and Item C07 (Warehouse W-3, 120 A load).

### 3.3 Cable Pulling Tension & Sidewall Bearing Pressure Analysis

## 3. ELECTRICAL ENGINEERING DESIGN & SYSTEM CALCULATIONS
### 3.1 Load Sizing, Ampacity & Thermal Modeling
Conductor sizing is established through rigorous thermal modeling adhering to Neher-McGrath methodology, IEEE 835, and NEC Article 310.60. 
- **Underground Ductbanks:** Soil thermal resistivity ($rho$) = 90 °C-cm/W (geotechnical baseline); ambient earth temperature = 20 °C; maximum continuous conductor operating temperature = 90 °C.
- **Feeder Load Factors (IEDS 2.3):** C01 and C02 serve critical command facilities (MB-1) and are evaluated at 100% continuous load factor (giving 335 A ampacity per set for 500 kcmil AL in 2x2 ductbank). C03, C04, C06, and C07 are evaluated at 75% load factor (giving 410 A for 500 kcmil AL and 300 A for 250 kcmil AL in 1x2 ductbank).
- **Riser Poles & Conduits in Air:** NEC Table 310.60(C)(71) / Table B.310.15(B)(2)(11) derated for 40 °C ambient summer temperature: 500 kcmil AL provides 245 A in enclosed interior conduit (C05); 250 kcmil AL provides 196 A in vertical pole risers (C06).
- **Overhead Conductor:** 1/0 AWG ACSR 'Raven' evaluated per IEEE 738 (40 °C ambient, 2 ft/s crosswind, 90 °C conductor temp) yields an ampacity of 242 A, easily exceeding the 40 A design load of Gate House GH-1.

### 3.2 Short-Circuit Thermal Withstand Analysis
Per PCSFA-IEDS Clause 2.4, medium-voltage cable conductors must withstand available short-circuit currents for the backup fault clearing time without exceeding maximum insulation damage temperatures (250 °C for XLPE/EPR insulation).

Per Protective Device Settings Schedule Rev D, the available three-phase symmetrical fault current at the 13.8 kV site substation SS-1 bus is **25.1 kA**, and the upstream feeder backup overcurrent clearing time is **0.16 seconds** (9.6 cycles).

The minimum conductor cross-sectional area is determined by the ICEA P-32-382 / Onderdonk short-circuit formula for aluminum conductors with thermoset insulation:
$$I_{sc} = A x sqrt{{0.0125}{t} log_{10}\left({T_2 + 228}{T_1 + 228}ight)}$$

Where:
- $I_{sc} = 25,100{ A}$ (fault current)
- $t = 0.16{ s}$ (clearing time)
- $T_1 = 90{ }^\ deg {C}$ (maximum continuous operating temperature)
- $T_2 = 250{ }^\ deg {C}$ (maximum transient short-circuit temperature)
- ${T_2 + 228}{T_1 + 228} = {478}{318} = 1.50314$
- $\log_{10}(1.50314) = 0.17700$
- Factor: $sqrt{{0.0125  *  0.17700}{0.16}} = sqrt{0.013828} = 0.11759{ A/cmil}$

Solving for minimum conductor area $A$:
$$A_{min} = {25,100}{0.11759}  ~=  213,450{ cmil}  ~=  213.5{ kcmil}$$

**Engineering Consequence:** Standard conductor sizes are 4/0 AWG (211.6 kcmil), 250 kcmil, 350 kcmil, and 500 kcmil. Because 4/0 AWG AL (211.6 kcmil) is strictly below the 213.5 kcmil thermal withstand threshold, **250 kcmil AL is the absolute statutory minimum conductor size permitted on the PCSFA 13.8 kV distribution network**. This governs the sizing of Item C04 (Lift Station, 60 A load), Item C06 underground risers (40 A load), and Item C07 (Warehouse W-3, 120 A load).

### 3.3 Cable Pulling Tension & Sidewall Bearing Pressure Analysis
Cable pulling calculations have been performed for every pull of the recommended designs using classical pulling mechanics in accordance with IEEE 1185, EPRI EL-5036, and UFGS 33 71 02:
- Conductor pulling eye maximum allowable tension: $T_{max} = 0.008  *  {cmil}  *  N_{cond}$ (12,000 lb for 3x 1/C 500 kcmil AL; 6,000 lb for 3x 1/C 250 kcmil AL).
- Maximum allowable sidewall bearing pressure (SWBP): **600 lb/ft** (governed by approved submittal SUB-33 71 02-07 for copper tape-shielded medium-voltage cable, overriding catalogue ratings per IEDS 1.3).
- Effective coefficient of friction: $mu = 0.35$ with approved pulling lubricant in PVC/HDPE/RGS ducts.
- Straight section tension: $T_2 = T_1 + mu x w x L$
- Horizontal bend tension: $T_2 = T_1 x cosh(mu theta) + sqrt{T_1^2 + (w R)^2} x sinh(mu theta) ~= T_1 x e^{mu theta}$
- Sidewall bearing pressure: $SWBP = {T_{out}}{R}$
- Conduit fill limit: 40% maximum for three conductors (NEC Chapter 9 Table 1).
- Jam ratio ($D/d$): Recommended safe bands are $<2.8$ or $>3.2$ to eliminate triplexed cable wedging during pulling around elbows.

## 3. ELECTRICAL ENGINEERING DESIGN & SYSTEM CALCULATIONS
### 3.1 Load Sizing, Ampacity & Thermal Modeling
Conductor sizing is established through rigorous thermal modeling adhering to Neher-McGrath methodology, IEEE 835, and NEC Article 310.60. 
- **Underground Ductbanks:** Soil thermal resistivity ($rho$) = 90 °C-cm/W (geotechnical baseline); ambient earth temperature = 20 °C; maximum continuous conductor operating temperature = 90 °C.
- **Feeder Load Factors (IEDS 2.3):** C01 and C02 serve critical command facilities (MB-1) and are evaluated at 100% continuous load factor (giving 335 A ampacity per set for 500 kcmil AL in 2x2 ductbank). C03, C04, C06, and C07 are evaluated at 75% load factor (giving 410 A for 500 kcmil AL and 300 A for 250 kcmil AL in 1x2 ductbank).
- **Riser Poles & Conduits in Air:** NEC Table 310.60(C)(71) / Table B.310.15(B)(2)(11) derated for 40 °C ambient summer temperature: 500 kcmil AL provides 245 A in enclosed interior conduit (C05); 250 kcmil AL provides 196 A in vertical pole risers (C06).
- **Overhead Conductor:** 1/0 AWG ACSR 'Raven' evaluated per IEEE 738 (40 °C ambient, 2 ft/s crosswind, 90 °C conductor temp) yields an ampacity of 242 A, easily exceeding the 40 A design load of Gate House GH-1.

### 3.2 Short-Circuit Thermal Withstand Analysis
Per PCSFA-IEDS Clause 2.4, medium-voltage cable conductors must withstand available short-circuit currents for the backup fault clearing time without exceeding maximum insulation damage temperatures (250 °C for XLPE/EPR insulation).

Per Protective Device Settings Schedule Rev D, the available three-phase symmetrical fault current at the 13.8 kV site substation SS-1 bus is **25.1 kA**, and the upstream feeder backup overcurrent clearing time is **0.16 seconds** (9.6 cycles).

The minimum conductor cross-sectional area is determined by the ICEA P-32-382 / Onderdonk short-circuit formula for aluminum conductors with thermoset insulation:
$$I_{sc} = A x sqrt{{0.0125}{t} log_{10}\left({T_2 + 228}{T_1 + 228}ight)}$$

Where:
- $I_{sc} = 25,100{ A}$ (fault current)
- $t = 0.16{ s}$ (clearing time)
- $T_1 = 90{ }^\ deg {C}$ (maximum continuous operating temperature)
- $T_2 = 250{ }^\ deg {C}$ (maximum transient short-circuit temperature)
- ${T_2 + 228}{T_1 + 228} = {478}{318} = 1.50314$
- $\log_{10}(1.50314) = 0.17700$
- Factor: $sqrt{{0.0125  *  0.17700}{0.16}} = sqrt{0.013828} = 0.11759{ A/cmil}$

Solving for minimum conductor area $A$:
$$A_{min} = {25,100}{0.11759}  ~=  213,450{ cmil}  ~=  213.5{ kcmil}$$

**Engineering Consequence:** Standard conductor sizes are 4/0 AWG (211.6 kcmil), 250 kcmil, 350 kcmil, and 500 kcmil. Because 4/0 AWG AL (211.6 kcmil) is strictly below the 213.5 kcmil thermal withstand threshold, **250 kcmil AL is the absolute statutory minimum conductor size permitted on the PCSFA 13.8 kV distribution network**. This governs the sizing of Item C04 (Lift Station, 60 A load), Item C06 underground risers (40 A load), and Item C07 (Warehouse W-3, 120 A load).

### 3.3 Cable Pulling Tension & Sidewall Bearing Pressure Analysis
Cable pulling calculations have been performed for every pull of the recommended designs using classical pulling mechanics in accordance with IEEE 1185, EPRI EL-5036, and UFGS 33 71 02:
- Conductor pulling eye maximum allowable tension: $T_{max} = 0.008  *  {cmil}  *  N_{cond}$ (12,000 lb for 3x 1/C 500 kcmil AL; 6,000 lb for 3x 1/C 250 kcmil AL).
- Maximum allowable sidewall bearing pressure (SWBP): **600 lb/ft** (governed by approved submittal SUB-33 71 02-07 for copper tape-shielded medium-voltage cable, overriding catalogue ratings per IEDS 1.3).
- Effective coefficient of friction: $mu = 0.35$ with approved pulling lubricant in PVC/HDPE/RGS ducts.
- Straight section tension: $T_2 = T_1 + mu x w x L$
- Horizontal bend tension: $T_2 = T_1 x cosh(mu theta) + sqrt{T_1^2 + (w R)^2} x sinh(mu theta) ~= T_1 x e^{mu theta}$
- Sidewall bearing pressure: $SWBP = {T_{out}}{R}$
- Conduit fill limit: 40% maximum for three conductors (NEC Chapter 9 Table 1).
- Jam ratio ($D/d$): Recommended safe bands are $<2.8$ or $>3.2$ to eliminate triplexed cable wedging during pulling around elbows.

Because 4/0 AWG AL (211.6 kcmil) is strictly below the 213.5 kcmil thermal withstand threshold, **250 kcmil AL is the absolute statutory minimum conductor size permitted on the PCSFA 13.8 kV distribution network**. This governs the sizing of Item C04 (Lift Station, 60 A load), Item C06 underground risers (40 A load), and Item C07 (Warehouse W-3, 120 A load).

### 3.3 Cable Pulling Tension & Sidewall Bearing Pressure Analysis
Cable pulling calculations have been performed for every pull of the recommended designs using classical pulling mechanics in accordance with IEEE 1185, EPRI EL-5036, and UFGS 33 71 02:

- Maximum allowable sidewall bearing pressure (SWBP): **600 lb/ft** (governed by approved submittal SUB-33 71 02-07 for copper tape-shielded medium-voltage cable, overriding catalogue ratings per IEDS 1.3).
- Effective coefficient of friction: $mu = 0.35$ with approved pulling lubricant in PVC/HDPE/RGS ducts.
- Straight section tension: $T_2 = T_1 + mu x w x L$
- Horizontal bend tension: $T_2 = T_1 x cosh(mu theta) + sqrt{T_1^2 + (w R)^2} x sinh(mu theta) ~= T_1 x e^{mu theta}$
- Sidewall bearing pressure: $SWBP = {T_{out}}{R}$
- Conduit fill limit: 40% maximum for three conductors (NEC Chapter 9 Table 1).
- Jam ratio ($D/d$): Recommended safe bands are $<2.8$ or $>3.2$ to eliminate triplexed cable wedging during pulling around elbows.

- **Feeder Load Factors (IEDS 2.3):** C01 and C02 serve critical command facilities (MB-1) and are evaluated at 100% continuous load factor (giving 335 A ampacity per set for 500 kcmil AL in 2x2 ductbank). C03, C04, C06, and C07 are evaluated at 75% load factor (giving 410 A for 500 kcmil AL and 300 A for 250 kcmil AL in 1x2 ductbank).
- **Riser Poles & Conduits in Air:** NEC Table 310.60(C)(71) / Table B.310.15(B)(2)(11) derated for 40 °C ambient summer temperature: 500 kcmil AL provides 245 A in enclosed interior conduit (C05); 250 kcmil AL provides 196 A in vertical pole risers (C06).
- **Overhead Conductor:** 1/0 AWG ACSR 'Raven' evaluated per IEEE 738 (40 °C ambient, 2 ft/s crosswind, 90 °C conductor temp) yields an ampacity of 242 A, easily exceeding the 40 A design load of Gate House GH-1.

### 3.2 Short-Circuit Thermal Withstand Analysis
Per PCSFA-IEDS Clause 2.4, medium-voltage cable conductors must withstand available short-circuit currents for the backup fault clearing time without exceeding maximum insulation damage temperatures (250 °C for XLPE/EPR insulation).

Per Protective Device Settings Schedule Rev D, the available three-phase symmetrical fault current at the 13.8 kV site substation SS-1 bus is **25.1 kA**, and the upstream feeder backup overcurrent clearing time is **0.16 seconds** (9.6 cycles).

The minimum conductor cross-sectional area is determined by the ICEA P-32-382 / Onderdonk short-circuit formula for aluminum conductors with thermoset insulation:
$$I_{sc} = A x sqrt{{0.0125}{t} log_{10}\left({T_2 + 228}{T_1 + 228}ight)}$$

Where:
- $I_{sc} = 25,100{ A}$ (fault current)
- $t = 0.16{ s}$ (clearing time)
- $T_1 = 90{ }^\ deg {C}$ (maximum continuous operating temperature)
- $T_2 = 250{ }^\ deg {C}$ (maximum transient short-circuit temperature)
- ${T_2 + 228}{T_1 + 228} = {478}{318} = 1.50314$
- $\log_{10}(1.50314) = 0.17700$
- Factor: $sqrt{{0.0125  *  0.17700}{0.16}} = sqrt{0.013828} = 0.11759{ A/cmil}$

Solving for minimum conductor area $A$:
$$A_{min} = {25,100}{0.11759}  ~=  213,450{ cmil}  ~=  213.5{ kcmil}$$

**Engineering Consequence:** Standard conductor sizes are 4/0 AWG (211.6 kcmil), 250 kcmil, 350 kcmil, and 500 kcmil. Because 4/0 AWG AL (211.6 kcmil) is strictly below the 213.5 kcmil thermal withstand threshold, **250 kcmil AL is the absolute statutory minimum conductor size permitted on the PCSFA 13.8 kV distribution network**. This governs the sizing of Item C04 (Lift Station, 60 A load), Item C06 underground risers (40 A load), and Item C07 (Warehouse W-3, 120 A load).

## 2. GOVERNING CRITERIA & HIERARCHY OF TRUTH
All engineering decisions and cost computations are governed strictly by the contract documents under the formal Order of Precedence established by PCSFA-IEDS Rev 3 Clause 1.3:
1. **Tier 1 (Highest Authority):** Project-specific RFP Amendments (RFP Section 01 11 00 Amd 0002), Approved Submittals (SUB-33 71 02-07), Protective Device Settings Schedule Rev D, SUE Utility Survey SUE-24-0117, and Arborist Survey TS-24-0117.
2. **Tier 2:** PCSFA Installation Electrical Design Standard (PCSFA-IEDS Rev 3, 2026-05-15).
3. **Tier 3:** DoD Unified Facilities Criteria: UFC 3-550-01 (*Exterior Electrical Power Distribution*, with Change 3, 2024), UFC 3-740-05 (*Construction Cost Estimating*, 2022 C1), and Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS 33 71 02, UFGS 26 05 00).
4. **Tier 4:** Federal Safety Regulations: OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P (*Excavations*); 29 CFR 1.6 (*Davis-Bacon Wage Determinations*).
5. **Tier 5:** Civil and Architectural Site Drawings (C-101, E-101, A-501) and Geotechnical Report GEO-24-0117 (with primary boring logs governing over summary tables).
6. **Tier 6 (Lowest Authority):** Preliminary/Reference estimates and manufacturer catalogue sheets.

### Permissibility Rules by Conveyance Typology:
- **Concrete-Encased Ductbank (CEDB):** Governed by UFC 3-550-01 Clause 3-11.2.1 and PCSFA-IEDS 4.2. CEDB is the required standard for all primary underground distribution circuits at PCSFA. Minimum burial depth is 30 in (24 in under paved surfaces). Spacers at 5-ft centers maintain 3-in inter-duct separation and 3-in concrete encasement on all sides. Minimum 1/3 spare duct capacity is mandated (50% provided via 2x2 and 1x2 banks).
- **Unencased Conduit Ductbank (UEDB):** Governed by PCSFA-IEDS 4.2 and UFC 3-550-01 3-11.2.1. Strictly prohibited for primary medium-voltage distribution across the Annex. Permitted only for low-voltage secondary circuits (<600 V) or telecommunications.
- **Direct-Buried Cable (DBC):** Governed by PCSFA-IEDS 4.2 and UFC 3-550-01 3-11.2.1 / 3-11.3.1. Prohibited for permanent 13.8 kV distribution due to high failure rates, lack of mechanical protection against excavation strikes, and inability to replace cables without trenching.
- **Horizontal Directional Drilling (HDD) as Sole Run Method:** Governed by PCSFA-IEDS 4.3 and UFC 3-550-01 3-11.4.1. HDD is permitted exclusively for discrete localized obstacle crossings (roads, drainage channels, rail tracks) where open-cut trenching is unacceptable. Continuous HDD for entire feeder runs is excluded due to thermal de-rating from deep placement (>10 ft), risk of bore deviation, inability to install intermediate manholes, and prohibitive cost.
- **Overhead Pole Lines (OH):** Governed by PCSFA-IEDS 4.1. Overhead lines are strictly prohibited within the industrial core and crane operating areas (bounded by the polygon north of y=350, east of x=250, west of x=1600). Overhead construction is permitted only along the southern utility corridor (y=220) serving remote facilities such as Gate House GH-1.
- **Interior Building Raceways (C05):** Governed by PCSFA-IEDS 5.1, NEC 300.37, and UFC 3-520-01. Rigid Metal Conduit (RMC) is permitted. Electrical Metallic Tubing (EMT) is prohibited for systems operating above 600 V. Cable tray (TRAY-EN and TRAY-LD) is prohibited due to geometric interference with HVAC ductwork in Corridor COR-1 (<18 in clearance to ceiling joists) and strict security keep-out requirements around SCIF IT-1.

## 3. ELECTRICAL ENGINEERING DESIGN & SYSTEM CALCULATIONS
### 3.1 Load Sizing, Ampacity & Thermal Modeling
Conductor sizing is established through rigorous thermal modeling adhering to Neher-McGrath methodology, IEEE 835, and NEC Article 310.60. 
- **Underground Ductbanks:** Soil thermal resistivity ($rho$) = 90 °C-cm/W (geotechnical baseline); ambient earth temperature = 20 °C; maximum continuous conductor operating temperature = 90 °C.
- **Feeder Load Factors (IEDS 2.3):** C01 and C02 serve critical command facilities (MB-1) and are evaluated at 100% continuous load factor (giving 335 A ampacity per set for 500 kcmil AL in 2x2 ductbank). C03, C04, C06, and C07 are evaluated at 75% load factor (giving 410 A for 500 kcmil AL and 300 A for 250 kcmil AL in 1x2 ductbank).
- **Riser Poles & Conduits in Air:** NEC Table 310.60(C)(71) / Table B.310.15(B)(2)(11) derated for 40 °C ambient summer temperature: 500 kcmil AL provides 245 A in enclosed interior conduit (C05); 250 kcmil AL provides 196 A in vertical pole risers (C06).
- **Overhead Conductor:** 1/0 AWG ACSR 'Raven' evaluated per IEEE 738 (40 °C ambient, 2 ft/s crosswind, 90 °C conductor temp) yields an ampacity of 242 A, easily exceeding the 40 A design load of Gate House GH-1.

### 3.2 Short-Circuit Thermal Withstand Analysis
Per PCSFA-IEDS Clause 2.4, medium-voltage cable conductors must withstand available short-circuit currents for the backup fault clearing time without exceeding maximum insulation damage temperatures (250 °C for XLPE/EPR insulation).

Per Protective Device Settings Schedule Rev D, the available three-phase symmetrical fault current at the 13.8 kV site substation SS-1 bus is **25.1 kA**, and the upstream feeder backup overcurrent clearing time is **0.16 seconds** (9.6 cycles).

The minimum conductor cross-sectional area is determined by the ICEA P-32-382 / Onderdonk short-circuit formula for aluminum conductors with thermoset insulation:
$$I_{sc} = A x sqrt{{0.0125}{t} log_{10}\left({T_2 + 228}{T_1 + 228}ight)}$$

Where:
- $I_{sc} = 25,100{ A}$ (fault current)
- $t = 0.16{ s}$ (clearing time)
- $T_1 = 90{ }^\ deg {C}$ (maximum continuous operating temperature)
- $T_2 = 250{ }^\ deg {C}$ (maximum transient short-circuit temperature)
- ${T_2 + 228}{T_1 + 228} = {478}{318} = 1.50314$
- $\log_{10}(1.50314) = 0.17700$
- Factor: $sqrt{{0.0125  *  0.17700}{0.16}} = sqrt{0.013828} = 0.11759{ A/cmil}$

Solving for minimum conductor area $A$:
$$A_{min} = {25,100}{0.11759}  ~=  213,450{ cmil}  ~=  213.5{ kcmil}$$

**Engineering Consequence:** Standard conductor sizes are 4/0 AWG (211.6 kcmil), 250 kcmil, 350 kcmil, and 500 kcmil. Because 4/0 AWG AL (211.6 kcmil) is strictly below the 213.5 kcmil thermal withstand threshold, **250 kcmil AL is the absolute statutory minimum conductor size permitted on the PCSFA 13.8 kV distribution network**. This governs the sizing of Item C04 (Lift Station, 60 A load), Item C06 underground risers (40 A load), and Item C07 (Warehouse W-3, 120 A load).

### 3.3 Cable Pulling Tension & Sidewall Bearing Pressure Analysis
Cable pulling calculations have been performed for every pull of the recommended designs using classical pulling mechanics in accordance with IEEE 1185, EPRI EL-5036, and UFGS 33 71 02:
- Conductor pulling eye maximum allowable tension: $T_{max} = 0.008  *  {cmil}  *  N_{cond}$ (12,000 lb for 3x 1/C 500 kcmil AL; 6,000 lb for 3x 1/C 250 kcmil AL).
- Maximum allowable sidewall bearing pressure (SWBP): **600 lb/ft** (governed by approved submittal SUB-33 71 02-07 for copper tape-shielded medium-voltage cable, overriding catalogue ratings per IEDS 1.3).
- Effective coefficient of friction: $mu = 0.35$ with approved pulling lubricant in PVC/HDPE/RGS ducts.
- Straight section tension: $T_2 = T_1 + mu x w x L$
- Horizontal bend tension: $T_2 = T_1 x cosh(mu theta) + sqrt{T_1^2 + (w R)^2} x sinh(mu theta) ~= T_1 x e^{mu theta}$
- Sidewall bearing pressure: $SWBP = {T_{out}}{R}$
- Conduit fill limit: 40% maximum for three conductors (NEC Chapter 9 Table 1).
- Jam ratio ($D/d$): Recommended safe bands are $<2.8$ or $>3.2$ to eliminate triplexed cable wedging during pulling around elbows.

2. **Tier 2:** PCSFA Installation Electrical Design Standard (PCSFA-IEDS Rev 3, 2026-05-15).
3. **Tier 3:** DoD Unified Facilities Criteria: UFC 3-550-01 (*Exterior Electrical Power Distribution*, with Change 3, 2024), UFC 3-740-05 (*Construction Cost Estimating*, 2022 C1), and Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS 33 71 02, UFGS 26 05 00).
4. **Tier 4:** Federal Safety Regulations: OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P (*Excavations*); 29 CFR 1.6 (*Davis-Bacon Wage Determinations*).
5. **Tier 5:** Civil and Architectural Site Drawings (C-101, E-101, A-501) and Geotechnical Report GEO-24-0117 (with primary boring logs governing over summary tables).
6. **Tier 6 (Lowest Authority):** Preliminary/Reference estimates and manufacturer catalogue sheets.

### Permissibility Rules by Conveyance Typology:
- **Concrete-Encased Ductbank (CEDB):** Governed by UFC 3-550-01 Clause 3-11.2.1 and PCSFA-IEDS 4.2. CEDB is the required standard for all primary underground distribution circuits at PCSFA. Minimum burial depth is 30 in (24 in under paved surfaces). Spacers at 5-ft centers maintain 3-in inter-duct separation and 3-in concrete encasement on all sides. Minimum 1/3 spare duct capacity is mandated (50% provided via 2x2 and 1x2 banks).
- **Unencased Conduit Ductbank (UEDB):** Governed by PCSFA-IEDS 4.2 and UFC 3-550-01 3-11.2.1. Strictly prohibited for primary medium-voltage distribution across the Annex. Permitted only for low-voltage secondary circuits (<600 V) or telecommunications.
- **Direct-Buried Cable (DBC):** Governed by PCSFA-IEDS 4.2 and UFC 3-550-01 3-11.2.1 / 3-11.3.1. Prohibited for permanent 13.8 kV distribution due to high failure rates, lack of mechanical protection against excavation strikes, and inability to replace cables without trenching.
- **Horizontal Directional Drilling (HDD) as Sole Run Method:** Governed by PCSFA-IEDS 4.3 and UFC 3-550-01 3-11.4.1. HDD is permitted exclusively for discrete localized obstacle crossings (roads, drainage channels, rail tracks) where open-cut trenching is unacceptable. Continuous HDD for entire feeder runs is excluded due to thermal de-rating from deep placement (>10 ft), risk of bore deviation, inability to install intermediate manholes, and prohibitive cost.
- **Overhead Pole Lines (OH):** Governed by PCSFA-IEDS 4.1. Overhead lines are strictly prohibited within the industrial core and crane operating areas (bounded by the polygon north of y=350, east of x=250, west of x=1600). Overhead construction is permitted only along the southern utility corridor (y=220) serving remote facilities such as Gate House GH-1.
- **Interior Building Raceways (C05):** Governed by PCSFA-IEDS 5.1, NEC 300.37, and UFC 3-520-01. Rigid Metal Conduit (RMC) is permitted. Electrical Metallic Tubing (EMT) is prohibited for systems operating above 600 V. Cable tray (TRAY-EN and TRAY-LD) is prohibited due to geometric interference with HVAC ductwork in Corridor COR-1 (<18 in clearance to ceiling joists) and strict security keep-out requirements around SCIF IT-1.
